t:
(a) In General.—The Under Secretary, through the National Weather Service and other appropriate weather and climate programs in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, shall establish a National Integrated Drought Information System. 
    (b) System Functions.—The National Integrated Drought Information System shall—
        (1) provide an effective drought early warning system that—
            (A) is a comprehensive system that collects and integrates information on the key indicators of drought in order to make usable, reliable, and timely drought forecasts and assessments of drought, including assessments of the severity of drought conditions and impacts; 
            (B) communicates drought forecasts, drought conditions, and drought impacts on an ongoing basis to—
                (i) decisionmakers at the Federal, regional, State, tribal, and local levels of government; 
                (ii) the private sector; and 
                (iii) the public,   in order to engender better informed and more timely decisions thereby leading to reduced impacts and costs; and
            (C) includes timely (where possible real-time) data, information, and products that reflect local, regional, and State differences in drought conditions;  
        (2) coordinate, and integrate as practicable, Federal research in support of a drought early warning system; and 
        (3) build upon existing forecasting and assessment programs and partnerships.  
    (c) Consultation.—The Under Secretary shall consult with relevant Federal, regional, State, tribal, and local government agencies, research institutions, and the private sector in the development of the National Integrated Drought Information System. 
    (d) Cooperation From Other Federal Agencies.—Each Federal agency shall cooperate as appropriate with the Under Secretary in carrying out this Act.

fable.w: Subsection (c) requires the Under Secretary to consult with State, tribal, and local governments, research institutions, and the private sector, all outside the federal government, in developing the federal drought information system. The tempting "No" reading treats the section as one-way dissemination of forecasts to the public (subsection (b)) or as purely intra-federal cooperation (subsection (d)). That reading fails because subsection (c) separately mandates consultation with non-federal parties on a federal action.
fable.s: The Under Secretary shall consult with relevant Federal, regional, State, tribal, and local government agencies, research institutions, and the private sector in the development of the National Integrated Drought Information System.

opus.w: Subsection (c) requires a federal official to consult non-federal parties (state, tribal and local governments, research institutions and the private sector) before deciding how to design the National Integrated Drought Information System. That brings outsiders into a federal decision. Sending forecasts to the public and requiring federal agencies to cooperate would not count on their own, but this consultation requirement does.
opus.s: (c) Consultation.—The Under Secretary shall consult with relevant Federal, regional, State, tribal, and local government agencies, research institutions, and the private sector in the development of the National Integrated Drought Information System.
opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting wrong reading.** Most of the section is one-way communication. Subsection (b)(1)(B) has the System send drought forecasts to states, tribes, the private sector and the public. Sending information out is not participation, and subsection (d) only covers cooperation among federal agencies, which stays inside the government. Subsection (c) is different. It requires the Under Secretary to consult outside parties (state, tribal and local governments, research institutions and the private sector) while developing the System. That is a federal decision, so the consultation crosses the federal boundary.

**Step 2: Label**

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Under Secretary to consult with entities outside the federal government, specifically State, tribal, and local government agencies, research institutions, and the private sector, before developing the National Integrated Drought Information System. This fits the definition of participation as it involves coordination with non-federal parties prior to a federal decision/action. The inclusion of federal agencies in the list does not negate the participation aspect because non-federal actors are explicitly included.
qwen_chat.s: (c) Consultation.—The Under Secretary shall consult with relevant Federal, regional, State, tribal, and local government agencies, research institutions, and the private sector in the development of the National Integrated Drought Information System.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the consultation in subsection (c) is merely internal coordination because it involves "Federal... agencies" alongside other entities. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation with states, tribes, local governments, research institutions, and the private sector constitutes participation, regardless of whether federal agencies are also involved. The presence of non-federal actors (states, tribes, private sector) in the consultation process for a federal decision (development of the system) triggers the "Yes" label.
